content.title: About
content.content: Chickpeas are a legume whose dried seeds are widely used in cooking. In this product a plant fat has been added, increasing its energy value and enhancing flavor. Chickpeas are rich in protein, fiber, and complex carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpeas are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown in ancient Egypt.
Dried chickpeas can be stored for up to a year when kept properly.
Added fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
Chickpeas are a staple in vegetarian and vegan dishes as a protein source.
In some cultures chickpeas are a symbol of hospitality.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpeas contain about 20 % protein, providing a valuable source of essential amino acids for plant‑based diets.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports regular bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The carbs in chickpeas are digested slowly, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: The added plant fat supplies unsaturated fatty acids that are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Chickpeas provide iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chickpeas.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking before cooking is recommended.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Added fat raises the calorie count, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause bloating and gas in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried chickpeas with added fat can be boiled, stewed, added to soups, stews, salads, or made into hummus. Soaking for 8–12 hours before cooking reduces cooking time and lowers phytic acid levels.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chickpeas in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
